givens: Balls of 1, 5, 2, 6, 3 and 4 g lie at the corners A to F of a hexagon, in this order.
The balls at two opposite corners were swapped: A and D, B and E, or C and F.

options: The balls at A and B against the balls at C and D
The ball at A against the ball at D
The ball at B against the ball at E
The balls at A and E against the ball at D
No one weighing can do it

statement.text: Six balls that look alike lie at the corners A to F of a hexagon, in this order round it. The ball at A weighs 1 g, at B 5 g, at C 2 g, at D 6 g, at E 3 g and at F 4 g. A joker has swapped the balls at two opposite corners: A and D, B and E, or C and F. Which one weighing on a balance without weights is sure to show which two were swapped?

task.unknown: The one weighing that is sure to show which two were swapped.

givens: Weights of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 and 80 g lie on the two pans, and one pan is heavier.
Seven children take weights away one at a time, and each time the other pan becomes the heavier.

statement.text: Eight weights of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 and 80 g lie on the two pans of a balance, and one pan is heavier. Seven children take the weights away one at a time. Every time a child takes a weight, the other pan becomes the heavier one. Which weight can be left on the balance at the end?

task.unknown: Which weight can be left at the end.
